correctness.rationale: For a shore A of size at least 3, S=A\{u,w1,w2} witnesses closure exchange failure: u not in cl(S), u in cl(S+{w1}), w1 not in cl(S+{u}); cases b>=3 and b=2 are separately checked in the proof. Exceptions are uniform-matroid direct sums, P4 loops, or free matroid, with exact closure. The standalone checker fully enumerates every seed for 45 small graphs, 1,482 large symbolic witness instances, and star exceptions. Finite tests corroborate, but the all-order proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 primary result proves only nonclosure under some edge deletion, whereas this theorem gives an all-parameter if-and-only-if for single-edge-deleted bicliques with uniform exchange witnesses and full exceptional matroids. Earlier undeleted biclique matroidality, minimum forcing numbers, crown graph enumerators, ordinary forcing, and cut-complex literature do not imply it. Priority remains provisional for unindexed equivalent work.
residual_risks: Historical priority: an unindexed or differently named classification of one-edge-deleted biclique skew-closure exchange could exist.
Literature discovery is not exhaustive and published-finding corpus semantic search is not an independence certificate.

value.rationale: This is an exact structural stability boundary in a canonical infinite graph family, not merely a zero-forcing-number computation or a single bad example: deleting any one edge turns every genuine biclique beyond the 2-by-2 exception from matroidal to nonmatroidal, whereas all star boundaries and the 4-path remain matroidal. This advances the explicit graph-class classification problem motivated by the 2026 matroidality paper and identifies the exceptional matroids.
